newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO official warns against selling Jews property.
newsitem.headline: PLO official warns against selling Jews property.

text.p: A top Islamic religious official in Jerusalem, the PLO-appointed mufti, warned Palestinians on Sunday to be wary of attempts by foreign front companies to buy their property on behalf of Jews.

"Do not sell your houses even to a Moslem... without referring to an Islamic institution like the Islamic Waqf (Trust) to ensure it is not handed over to Jews," Mufti Ikrima Sabri said in a statement published in Arabic newspapers.

He said the Waqf had information that since the 1980s "foreign companies with Zionist capital" had been established to buy Palestinian homes and land and the deeds were then transferred to "extremist Jewish groups based in Jerusalem".

Israel Radio reported on Sunday that a group of Jews living abroad was behind a campaign to buy as much land in the occupied territories as possible ahead of Israel-PLO talks on a final peace agreement.
The radio said the group had raised $35 million to fund the campaign.
Sabri said the foreign companies, which he did not identify, had tricked Palestinian land owners by representing themselves as charity organisations rendering services to Arabs.
He said the Waqf recently stopped three deals from being finalised to sell Palestinian property to Israelis in Jerusalem's Old City and nearby al-Thori neighbourhoud.
Palestinians have largely refrained from selling their property to Israelis for fear of extending Israeli presence amidst Arabs in the West Bank, including Arab East Jerusalem.
There are around 3,000 Jews living in East Jerusalem's Old City amidst 30,000 Palestinians.
